The cardinality of a finite set $A$ is the number of elements in $A.$ 

Notice that the elements of our set 

$$
98,\,102,\,106,\,…
$$

form an arithmetic sequence with a common difference $d=4:$

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =4 \\  & =102-98 \\  & =106-102 \\  & =⋯\end{aligned}
$$

The $n$th term of our arithmetic sequence, denoted ${a}_{n},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =98+(n-1)\cdot 4 \\  & =98+4n-4 \\  & =4n+94.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can express $A$ in set-builder notation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={4n+94:n\in N,\,1\le n\le N}\end{aligned}
$$

where $N\in N$ is to be determined.

To find $N,$ we solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}4N+94 & =810 \\ 4N & =716 \\ N & =\frac{716}{4} \\ N & =179\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ can be expressed as

$$
A={4n+94:n\in N,\,1\le n\le 179}.
$$

Finally, since $A$ has $179$ elements, we must have $|A|=179.$
